steps.title: Check the actual copy and terms
steps.instruction: Use an already permitted noncommercial completed build from the currently licensed Toshinden source. Preserve the project, framework and component notices. This does not establish permission for arbitrary older v0.1.3 packages.

steps.title: Finish upstream setup with your originals
steps.instruction: Finish supported upstream Generate & Build with your own USA SCUS-94200 original outside Portcove. Keep the CUE and all fourteen BIN tracks together. The data track is 14,662,368 bytes, SHA-1 cb03e66d2a5e68f402f9c64741a94c02ca78d4c5; retain the complete TOC/source set, not just that track. Establish a working completed product before registration.

steps.title: Select the completed player
steps.instruction: Choose build-release/BattleArenaToshinden_Recompiled.exe, with its containing completed product folder as the working directory. Do not choose the zip-root/setup-host executable: setup-host forwarding runs before argument parsing, so --no-launcher alone does not bypass it.

steps.title: Preserve your established source and save coordinates
steps.instruction: For the ordinary direct route use three literal argument tokens: --no-launcher, --disc, and the absolute path to your supported USA CUE. Keep spaces inside the CUE path token. Preserve the working copy's existing BIOS choice, card/state/settings and custom locations. Do not add a new --memcard-dir merely to register: it clears explicit custom slot paths. Retain that override only if it was already part of your established working invocation, with its exact existing directory.

steps.title: Review, consent, Play and preserve ownership
steps.instruction: Review the exact executable, working directory and literal arguments and consent to that execution intent. Registration does not start the game; choose Play separately. Portcove retains registration/relink across restart and observes the selected process. Upstream/player own preparation, repair and runtime replacement. Close every actual player and preserve all files before upstream changes. Removing the registration removes only Portcove metadata and preserves every external file.

warnings: Preserve all originals/tracks, generated runtime and source, BIOS files and notices, executable-parent settings.toml, config.ini, input.ini, keybinds.ini, mods/state, diagnostics/heartbeat, cache/captures and every actual custom card/state/profile path. --memcard-dir is not an all-writes redirect. A different executable folder can change active settings; registration does not migrate data or prove state compatibility. Keep quickstates with their creating runtime; unchanged originals or current licensing do not establish build-state compatibility.

Configured setup/rebuild, overlay compiler/toolchain/command modes and relaunches remain upstream-owned. The ordinary direct player is the selected process; successors can require separate closure. Registration is not a sandbox or an exclusive lock over all external players. Network/debug behavior depends on the build, settings and environment; no offline/no-listener, netplay or public-relay qualification is promised.

Core does not authenticate the disc set, generated code, component rights or build provenance. Managed acquisition, Install, Update, Backup, Rollback, migration and external deletion are unoffered. Gameplay/save-load, new native game runs, other platforms and installed/protected-client delivery remain unqualified by this route.
